parsed.study_design: Exploratory mixed-methods study combining a cross-sectional questionnaire, qualitative thematic content analysis, and observational time measurement
parsed.population_and_sample: Questionnaire respondents recruited primarily among university students and additionally through social media (N=97: 70 women and 27 men); 30 provided evaluable open-ended responses. The observational phase measured 24 male and 32 female public-toilet users at Széchenyi István University in Gyor.
parsed.exposure: Public-toilet provision and governance conditions, including facility availability and capacity, queues, hygiene and maintenance, privacy and safety, care-related facilities, and gendered regulatory or planning standards.
parsed.outcome: Access barriers, perceived safety and satisfaction, inability to use facilities or meet childcare needs, reliance on paid or commercial alternatives, waiting and time costs, and observed restroom-use duration.
parsed.rationale: The Methods section (pp. 5–6) identifies an exploratory mixed-methods design using a questionnaire, open-ended responses, and direct observation of restroom-use duration. The Findings (pp. 6–10) report empirical access outcomes including safety, missing changing facilities, availability and queues, commercial workarounds, and gender-disaggregated use times. Sections 4.1–4.4 (pp. 10–14) explicitly connect these outcomes to building standards, municipal planning, maintenance, service regulation, and institutional accountability.
